card: BAYES-OCCUPANCY-ANOMALY-NEVER-EVALUATES-1 (rebuilt on a dwell model, v5.103.83)
root_cause: Two causes. (1) It never evaluates: the logic is in async_update on a CoordinatorEntity that HA never polls. (2) Wiring it would not help: the Bayesian model counts ARRIVALS per time bin, not dwell, so long-stay rooms like Study A (20 h in 14 days, share 1.1%, p=0.004) would read 'unusual' during ordinary use.
root_cause_must_mention: async_update never called on a non-polling CoordinatorEntity
model counts arrivals not dwell, so long-dwell rooms look anomalous
correct_tier: propose (code; operator decision: retire or rebuild on a dwell model)
correct_actions: propose_action tier=code with both findings and the choice: retire, or rebuild on a time-occupied (dwell) model; do not just move the logic into the coordinator update
acceptable_extra: recommend measuring the would-fire rate first
wrong_actions: proposing only the wiring fix (moves logic to _handle_coordinator_update) as sufficient
proposing a lower threshold as the fix
invented_evidence_traps: Stating a would-fire rate per day (not in snapshot)
Claiming the predictor has no data
Claiming HA polls the entity every 30 s
partial_credit: Half root-cause credit for (1) alone; full needs (2).
discriminator: The wiring-only answer predicts a working sensor after the fix; Study A's 20 h dwell vs 1.1% share shows it would fire on normal use.
